title: Jesus, the All-restoring Word
description: Jesus, the All-restoring Word in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 169. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, the all re-stor-ing Word, My fall-en spi-rit's hope, Af-ter thy love-ly like-ness, Lord, Ah, when shall I wake up?

lines: Jesus, the all-restoring Word,
My fallen spirit's hope,
After thy lovely likeness, Lord,
Ah, when shall I wake up?
Thou, O my God, thou only art
The Life, the Truth, the Way;
Quicken my soul, instruct my heart.
My sinking, footsteps stay.
Of all thou hast in earth below,
In heaven above, to give,
Give me thy only love to know.
In thee to walk and live.
Fill me with all the life of love;
In mystic union join
Me to thyself, and let me prove
The fellowship divine.
Open the intercourse between
My longing soul and thee,
Never to be broke off again
To all eternity.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
